source_definition: Chronic systemic autoimmune disease characterised by inflammatory polyarthritis of the small joints, typically diagnosed and managed by rheumatologists in outpatient care.
clinical_rationale: Lifelong disease once diagnosed; serology (rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP) and DMARD initiation are expected shortly after diagnosis, with ongoing specialist follow-up.

source_definition: Supraventricular arrhythmia with uncoordinated atrial activation; episodes may be paroxysmal, persistent or permanent and are often first detected in emergency or inpatient settings.
clinical_rationale: Recurs over time with long symptom-free periods; ECG confirmation and rate or rhythm control or anticoagulation are expected, and follow-up visits are common.

source_definition: Acute bleeding anywhere in the gastrointestinal tract presenting with hematemesis, melena or hematochezia; usually evaluated in the emergency department and confirmed by endoscopy.
clinical_rationale: Discrete episodes that can recur; endoscopy and acid suppression or transfusion are expected around diagnosis. Episodes are short so a fixed 30 day exit is used.

source_definition: New-onset hypertension with proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction after 20 weeks of gestation that resolves after delivery.
clinical_rationale: Restricted to pregnant women of reproductive age; resolves within weeks of delivery so a fixed exit window is used.
